'''Daniel Gregg Santiago''' (born June 24, 1976) is a Puerto Rican [[basketball]] coach at [[IMG Academy]] and former professional player.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theringer.com/2023/3/15/23640235/zach-edey-purdue-boilermakers |title=Zach Edey Is Just Different |date=March 15, 2023 |publisher=theringer.com |access-date=March 16, 2023}}</ref> A [[Center (basketball)|center]], he had a collegiate career in the [[NCAA]] and [[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics|NAIA]]. His professional career saw him play in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]], the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] of [[Puerto Rico]], and overseas. Santiago has played for the [[Puerto Rico national basketball team|Puerto Rican national team]] since 1998 until 2014, including been part of the 2004 team that defeated the United States at the [[Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2004 Olympic Games]] in [[Greece]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usabasketball.com/seniormen/2004/04_moly1_box.html |title=Puerto Rico 92, USA 73 |publisher=Usabasketball.com |access-date=December 18, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111101085351/http://www.usabasketball.com/seniormen/2004/04_moly1_box.html |archive-date=November 1, 2011 }}</ref>

==College career==
Santiago attended and played Junior College basketball at [[New Mexico Military Institute]] in [[Roswell, New Mexico]] and played [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] Division I basketball at the [[University of New Mexico]]. He finished up his collegiate career at the [[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics|NAIA]] school of [[Saint Vincent College]] in [[Latrobe, Pennsylvania]], where he was named NAIA player of the year. In 2019 Daniel Santiago obtained a college degree in General Studies with concentrations in Social Work, Sociology and History from the University of South Florida.<ref>{{cite news |title=Santiago Is Player Of Year |url=http://business.highbeam.com/2872/article-1G1-107584285/santiago-player-year |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130918062103/http://business.highbeam.com/2872/article-1G1-107584285/santiago-player-year |archive-date=September 18, 2013 |via=[[HighBeam Research]] |url-access=subscription |url-status=usurped}}</ref>

==Professional career==
In [[Puerto Rico]], Santiago played professionally on the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|National Superior Basketball League]] with the ''[[Vaqueros de Bayamón|Vaqueros]]'', helping the team to various national championships and tournament finals.

Between 1998 and 2000, he played for [[Pallacanestro Varese|Varese Roosters]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A|Serie A]].

From 2000 to 2001 he played for the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]'s [[Phoenix Suns]] as a back-up center until being released.
He returned to the NBA in 2003, playing two seasons with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].

In 2005, Santiago signed for a season with [[Liga ACB|Spanish ACB League]]'s [[CB Málaga|Unicaja Málaga]]. After winning the [[2005–06 ACB season|2006 league]], he signed a further two-year deal with the [[Andalusia]] outfit. In 2008, Santiago signed with [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|Regal FC Barcelona]], helping the side to a third finish in the [[2008–09 Euroleague]].

In July 2009, Santiago came back to the BSN after a 7-year absence, joining the [[Bayamón Cowboys]]. In September 2009 he signed with [[Efes Pilsen S.K.]] of Turkey.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2009-10-signings/i/58107/3694/efes-pilsen-adds-power-with-daniel-santiago Santiago's latest transfer news]</ref> In October 2010 he signed with [[Spirou Charleroi]].<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2010-11-signings/i/77426/4465/spirou-gets-bigger-with-santiago SPIROU gets bigger with Santiago]</ref> In January 2011 he joined [[Capitanes de Arecibo]].<ref>[http://translate.googleusercontent.com/translate_c?hl=es&ie=UTF-8&sl=es&tl=en&u=https://twitter.com/fibaamericas/statuses/24937994653794305&prev=_t&rurl=translate.google.com&usg=ALkJrhgu25z8kmZPrkmpUe6Ls1FxrcYQNQ Daniel Santiago reports to the practices of the Arecibo Captains for the League of the Americas.]</ref>

In September 2012, Santiago signed with [[Boca Juniors (basketball)|Boca Juniors]] in Argentina.<ref>[https://www.latinbasket.com/Puerto-Rico/basketball.aspx?NewsID=287220 Daniel Santiago joins Boca Juniors]</ref> In March 2013, he was selected as the league's best center for the season.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20160305013345/http://www.fibaamericas.com/en/noticiasread4.asp?r=DDBF18F78AF24A11B7336DDCDA728927 ARG – The Best of the National League are awarded]</ref> In May 2013, he joined the [[Mets de Guaynabo (basketball)|Mets de Guaynabo]] in Puerto Rico.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.elnuevodia.com/decaminoalosmetsdeguaynaboelcentrodanielsantiago-1505444.html |title=De camino a los Mets de Guaynabo el centro Daniel Santiago |access-date=May 9, 2013 |archive-date=May 9, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130509155811/http://www.elnuevodia.com/decaminoalosmetsdeguaynaboelcentrodanielsantiago-1505444.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==National team career==
In 2002, Santiago represented senior the [[Puerto Rico national basketball team|Puerto Rican national team]] at the [[Indianapolis]] [[2002 FIBA World Cup]], and he also played in the [[Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2004 Summer Olympics]] team that handed the [[United States national basketball team|United States]] their first defeat in Olympic play, since they began using [[NBA]] players. Santiago again represented Puerto Rico at the [[2006 FIBA World Championship|2006 World Cup]]. He retired from the national side in 2007, only to return the following year.

==Personal==
Santiago's paternal grandfather, Pedro Santiago Rodríguez, was a well known [[baseball]] player in [[Puerto Rico]] and emigrated to the United States to play. Due to his small stature he was nicknamed "[[Jockey]]", while grandson Daniel received the "El Gigante" (the giant) moniker. Puerto Rico's Jockey Rodríguez retired from baseball with the Albuquerque Dukes team under the name Pedro Santiago.

Santiago was raised in the West [[Texas]] area of [[Lamesa, Texas|Lamesa]] on a cotton farm and later in [[Albuquerque, New Mexico]] where his parents, Stan and Diana Santiago, originated. He has two younger brothers, Matthew and Jarrett Santiago.
